    11	/// An expression, made up of nested operations and values. Values are either
    12	/// constants, or numeric column references which are looked up in rows.
    13	/// Evaluated to a final value during query execution.
    14	///
    15	/// Since this is a recursive data structure, we have to box each child
    16	/// expression, which incurs a heap allocation per expression node. There are
    17	/// clever ways to avoid this, but we keep it simple.
    18	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    19	pub enum Expression {
    20	    /// A constant value.
    21	    Constant(Value),
    22	    /// A column reference. Looks up the value in a row during evaluation.
    23	    Column(usize),
    24	
    25	    /// a AND b: logical AND of two booleans.
    26	    And(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),
    27	    /// a OR b: logical OR of two booleans.
    28	    Or(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),
    29	    /// NOT a: logical NOT of a boolean.
    30	    Not(Box<Expression>),
    31	
    32	    /// a = b: equality comparison of two values.
    33	    Equal(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),
    34	    /// Greater than comparison of two values: a > b.
    35	    GreaterThan(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),
    36	    /// a < b: less than comparison of two values.
    37	    LessThan(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),
    38	    /// a IS NULL or a IS NAN: checks for the given value.
    39	    Is(Box<Expression>, Value),
    40	
    41	    /// a + b: adds two numbers.
    42	    Add(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),
    43	    /// a / b: divides two numbers.
    44	    Divide(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),
    45	    /// a ^b: exponentiates two numbers.
    46	    Exponentiate(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),
    47	    /// a!: takes the factorial of a number (4! = 4*3*2*1).
    48	    Factorial(Box<Expression>),
    49	    /// +a: the identify function, which simply returns the same number.
    50	    Identity(Box<Expression>),
    51	    /// a * b: multiplies two numbers.
    52	    Multiply(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),
    53	    /// -a: negates the given number.
    54	    Negate(Box<Expression>),
    55	    /// a % b: the remainder after dividing two numbers.
    56	    Remainder(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),
    57	    /// √a: takes the square root of a number.
    58	    SquareRoot(Box<Expression>),
    59	    /// a - b: subtracts two numbers.
    60	    Subtract(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),
    61	
    62	    // a LIKE b: checks if a string matches a pattern.
    63	    Like(Box<Expression>, Box<Expression>),
    64	}
    65	
    66	impl Expression {
    67	    /// Displays the expression, using the given plan node to look up labels for
    68	    /// column references.
    69	    pub fn display<'a>(&'a self, node: &'a Node) -> ExpressionDisplay<'a> {
    70	        ExpressionDisplay::new(self, node, 0)
    71	    }
    72	
    73	    /// Evaluates an expression, returning a constant value. Column references
    74	    /// are looked up in the given row (or panic if the row is None).
    75	    pub fn evaluate(&self, row: Option<&Row>) -> Result<Value> {
    76	        use Value::*;
    77	
    78	        Ok(match self {
    79	            // Constant values return themselves.
    80	            Self::Constant(value) => value.clone(),
    81	
    82	            // Column references look up a row value. The planner ensures that
    83	            // only constant expressions are evaluated without a row.
    84	            Self::Column(index) => row.and_then(|r| r.get(*index)).cloned().expect("invalid index"),
    85	
    86	            // Logical AND. Inputs must be boolean or NULL. NULLs generally
    87	            // yield NULL, except the special case NULL AND false == false.
    88	            Self::And(lhs, rhs) => match (lhs.evaluate(row)?, rhs.evaluate(row)?) {
    89	                (Boolean(lhs), Boolean(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs && rhs),
    90	                (Boolean(b), Null) | (Null, Boolean(b)) if !b => Boolean(false),
    91	                (Boolean(_), Null) | (Null, Boolean(_)) | (Null, Null) => Null,
    92	                (lhs, rhs) => return errinput!("can't AND {lhs} and {rhs}"),
    93	            },
    94	
    95	            // Logical OR. Inputs must be boolean or NULL. NULLs generally
    96	            // yield NULL, except the special case NULL OR true == true.
    97	            Self::Or(lhs, rhs) => match (lhs.evaluate(row)?, rhs.evaluate(row)?) {
    98	                (Boolean(lhs), Boolean(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs || rhs),
    99	                (Boolean(b), Null) | (Null, Boolean(b)) if b => Boolean(true),
   100	                (Boolean(_), Null) | (Null, Boolean(_)) | (Null, Null) => Null,
   101	                (lhs, rhs) => return errinput!("can't OR {lhs} and {rhs}"),
   102	            },
   103	
   104	            // Logical NOT. Input must be boolean or NULL.
   105	            Self::Not(expr) => match expr.evaluate(row)? {
   106	                Boolean(b) => Boolean(!b),
   107	                Null => Null,
   108	                value => return errinput!("can't NOT {value}"),
   109	            },
   110	
   111	            // Comparisons. Must be of same type, except floats and integers
   112	            // which are interchangeable. NULLs yield NULL, NaNs yield NaN.
   113	            //
   114	            // Does not dispatch to Value.cmp() because comparison and sorting
   115	            // is different for Nulls and NaNs in SQL and code.
   116	            #[allow(clippy::float_cmp)]
   117	            Self::Equal(lhs, rhs) => match (lhs.evaluate(row)?, rhs.evaluate(row)?) {
   118	                (Boolean(lhs), Boolean(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs == rhs),
   119	                (Integer(lhs), Integer(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs == rhs),
   120	                (Integer(lhs), Float(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs as f64 == rhs),
   121	                (Float(lhs), Integer(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs == rhs as f64),
   122	                (Float(lhs), Float(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs == rhs),
   123	                (String(lhs), String(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs == rhs),
   124	                (Null, _) | (_, Null) => Null,
   125	                (lhs, rhs) => return errinput!("can't compare {lhs} and {rhs}"),
   126	            },
   127	
   128	            Self::GreaterThan(lhs, rhs) => match (lhs.evaluate(row)?, rhs.evaluate(row)?) {
   129	                #[allow(clippy::bool_comparison)]
   130	                (Boolean(lhs), Boolean(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs > rhs),
   131	                (Integer(lhs), Integer(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs > rhs),
   132	                (Integer(lhs), Float(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs as f64 > rhs),
   133	                (Float(lhs), Integer(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs > rhs as f64),
   134	                (Float(lhs), Float(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs > rhs),
   135	                (String(lhs), String(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs > rhs),
   136	                (Null, _) | (_, Null) => Null,
   137	                (lhs, rhs) => return errinput!("can't compare {lhs} and {rhs}"),
   138	            },
   139	
   140	            Self::LessThan(lhs, rhs) => match (lhs.evaluate(row)?, rhs.evaluate(row)?) {
   141	                #[allow(clippy::bool_comparison)]
   142	                (Boolean(lhs), Boolean(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs < rhs),
   143	                (Integer(lhs), Integer(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs < rhs),
   144	                (Integer(lhs), Float(rhs)) => Boolean((lhs as f64) < rhs),
   145	                (Float(lhs), Integer(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs < rhs as f64),
   146	                (Float(lhs), Float(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs < rhs),
   147	                (String(lhs), String(rhs)) => Boolean(lhs < rhs),
   148	                (Null, _) | (_, Null) => Null,
   149	                (lhs, rhs) => return errinput!("can't compare {lhs} and {rhs}"),
   150	            },
   151	
   152	            Self::Is(expr, Null) => Boolean(expr.evaluate(row)? == Null),
   153	            Self::Is(expr, Float(f)) if f.is_nan() => match expr.evaluate(row)? {
   154	                Float(f) => Boolean(f.is_nan()),
   155	                Null => Null,
   156	                v => return errinput!("IS NAN can't be used with {}", v.datatype().unwrap()),
   157	            },
   158	            Self::Is(_, v) => panic!("invalid IS value {v}"), // enforced by parser
   159	
   160	            // Mathematical operations. Inputs must be numbers, but integers and
   161	            // floats are interchangeable (float when mixed). NULLs yield NULL.
   162	            // Errors on integer overflow, but floats yield infinity or NaN.
   163	            Self::Add(lhs, rhs) => lhs.evaluate(row)?.checked_add(&rhs.evaluate(row)?)?,
   164	            Self::Divide(lhs, rhs) => lhs.evaluate(row)?.checked_div(&rhs.evaluate(row)?)?,
   165	            Self::Exponentiate(lhs, rhs) => lhs.evaluate(row)?.checked_pow(&rhs.evaluate(row)?)?,
   166	            Self::Factorial(expr) => match expr.evaluate(row)? {
   167	                Integer(i @ 0..) => {
   168	                    (1..=i).try_fold(Integer(1), |p, i| p.checked_mul(&Integer(i)))?
   169	                }
   170	                Null => Null,
   171	                value => return errinput!("can't take factorial of {value}"),
   172	            },
   173	            Self::Identity(expr) => match expr.evaluate(row)? {
   174	                value @ (Integer(_) | Float(_) | Null) => value,
   175	                expr => return errinput!("can't take the identity of {expr}"),
   176	            },
   177	            Self::Multiply(lhs, rhs) => lhs.evaluate(row)?.checked_mul(&rhs.evaluate(row)?)?,
   178	            Self::Negate(expr) => match expr.evaluate(row)? {
   179	                Integer(i) => Integer(-i),
   180	                Float(f) => Float(-f),
   181	                Null => Null,
   182	                value => return errinput!("can't negate {value}"),
   183	            },
   184	            Self::Remainder(lhs, rhs) => lhs.evaluate(row)?.checked_rem(&rhs.evaluate(row)?)?,
   185	            Self::SquareRoot(expr) => match expr.evaluate(row)? {
   186	                Integer(i @ 0..) => Float((i as f64).sqrt()),
   187	                Float(f) => Float(f.sqrt()),
   188	                Null => Null,
   189	                value => return errinput!("can't take square root of {value}"),
   190	            },
   191	            Self::Subtract(lhs, rhs) => lhs.evaluate(row)?.checked_sub(&rhs.evaluate(row)?)?,
   192	
   193	            // LIKE pattern matching, using _ and % as single- and
   194	            // multi-character wildcards. Inputs must be strings. NULLs yield
   195	            // NULL. There's no support for escaping an _ and %.
   196	            Self::Like(lhs, rhs) => match (lhs.evaluate(row)?, rhs.evaluate(row)?) {
   197	                (String(lhs), String(rhs)) => {
   198	                    // We could precompile the pattern if it's constant, instead
   199	                    // of recompiling it for every row, but we keep it simple.
   200	                    let pattern =
   201	                        format!("^{}$", regex::escape(&rhs).replace('%', ".*").replace('_', "."));
   202	                    Boolean(Regex::new(&pattern)?.is_match(&lhs))
   203	                }
   204	                (String(_), Null) | (Null, String(_)) | (Null, Null) => Null,
   205	                (lhs, rhs) => return errinput!("can't LIKE {lhs} and {rhs}"),
   206	            },
   207	        })
   208	    }

   210	    /// Recursively walks the expression tree depth-first, calling the given
   211	    /// closure until it returns false. Returns true otherwise.
   212	    pub fn walk(&self, visitor: &mut impl FnMut(&Expression) -> bool) -> bool {
   213	        if !visitor(self) {
   214	            return false;
   215	        }
   216	        match self {
   217	            Self::Add(lhs, rhs)
   218	            | Self::And(lhs, rhs)
   219	            | Self::Divide(lhs, rhs)
   220	            | Self::Equal(lhs, rhs)
   221	            | Self::Exponentiate(lhs, rhs)
   222	            | Self::GreaterThan(lhs, rhs)
   223	            | Self::LessThan(lhs, rhs)
   224	            | Self::Like(lhs, rhs)
   225	            | Self::Multiply(lhs, rhs)
   226	            | Self::Or(lhs, rhs)
   227	            | Self::Remainder(lhs, rhs)
   228	            | Self::Subtract(lhs, rhs) => lhs.walk(visitor) && rhs.walk(visitor),
   229	
   230	            Self::Factorial(expr)
   231	            | Self::Identity(expr)
   232	            | Self::Is(expr, _)
   233	            | Self::Negate(expr)
   234	            | Self::Not(expr)
   235	            | Self::SquareRoot(expr) => expr.walk(visitor),
   236	
   237	            Self::Constant(_) | Self::Column(_) => true,
   238	        }
   239	    }
   240	
   241	    /// Recursively walks the expression tree depth-first, calling the given
   242	    /// closure until it returns true. Returns false otherwise. This is the
   243	    /// inverse of walk().
   244	    pub fn contains(&self, visitor: &impl Fn(&Expression) -> bool) -> bool {
   245	        !self.walk(&mut |e| !visitor(e))
   246	    }
   247	
   248	    /// Transforms the expression by recursively applying the given closures
   249	    /// depth-first to each node before/after descending.
   250	    pub fn transform(
   251	        mut self,
   252	        before: &impl Fn(Self) -> Result<Self>,
   253	        after: &impl Fn(Self) -> Result<Self>,
   254	    ) -> Result<Self> {
   255	        // Helper for transforming boxed expressions.
   256	        let xform = |mut expr: Box<Expression>| -> Result<Box<Expression>> {
   257	            *expr = expr.transform(before, after)?;
   258	            Ok(expr)
   259	        };
   260	
   261	        self = before(self)?;
   262	        self = match self {
   263	            Self::Add(lhs, rhs) => Self::Add(xform(lhs)?, xform(rhs)?),
   264	            Self::And(lhs, rhs) => Self::And(xform(lhs)?, xform(rhs)?),
   265	            Self::Divide(lhs, rhs) => Self::Divide(xform(lhs)?, xform(rhs)?),
   266	            Self::Equal(lhs, rhs) => Self::Equal(xform(lhs)?, xform(rhs)?),
   267	            Self::Exponentiate(lhs, rhs) => Self::Exponentiate(xform(lhs)?, xform(rhs)?),
   268	            Self::GreaterThan(lhs, rhs) => Self::GreaterThan(xform(lhs)?, xform(rhs)?),
   269	            Self::LessThan(lhs, rhs) => Self::LessThan(xform(lhs)?, xform(rhs)?),
   270	            Self::Like(lhs, rhs) => Self::Like(xform(lhs)?, xform(rhs)?),
   271	            Self::Multiply(lhs, rhs) => Self::Multiply(xform(lhs)?, xform(rhs)?),
   272	            Self::Or(lhs, rhs) => Self::Or(xform(lhs)?, xform(rhs)?),
   273	            Self::Remainder(lhs, rhs) => Self::Remainder(xform(lhs)?, xform(rhs)?),
   274	            Self::SquareRoot(expr) => Self::SquareRoot(xform(expr)?),
   275	            Self::Subtract(lhs, rhs) => Self::Subtract(xform(lhs)?, xform(rhs)?),
   276	
   277	            Self::Factorial(expr) => Self::Factorial(xform(expr)?),
   278	            Self::Identity(expr) => Self::Identity(xform(expr)?),
   279	            Self::Is(expr, value) => Self::Is(xform(expr)?, value),
   280	            Self::Negate(expr) => Self::Negate(xform(expr)?),
   281	            Self::Not(expr) => Self::Not(xform(expr)?),
   282	
   283	            expr @ (Self::Constant(_) | Self::Column(_)) => expr,
   284	        };
   285	        self = after(self)?;
   286	        Ok(self)
   287	    }

   289	    /// Converts the expression into conjunctive normal form, i.e. an AND of
   290	    /// ORs, useful during plan optimization. This is done by converting to
   291	    /// negation normal form and then applying De Morgan's distributive law.
   292	    pub fn into_cnf(self) -> Self {
   293	        use Expression::{And, Or};
   294	
   295	        let xform = |expr| {
   296	            // Can't use a single match; needs deref patterns.
   297	            let Or(lhs, rhs) = expr else {
   298	                return expr;
   299	            };

   301	                // (x AND y) OR z → (x OR z) AND (y OR z)

   303	                // x OR (y AND z) → (x OR y) AND (x OR z)

   305	                // Otherwise, do nothing.
   306	                (lhs, rhs) => Or(lhs.into(), rhs.into()),
   307	            }
   308	        };
   309	        self.into_nnf().transform(&|e| Ok(xform(e)), &Ok).unwrap() // infallible
   310	    }

   313	    /// ANDed expressions (instead of nested ANDs).
